messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: p99 tail latency breach detected for customer 'Nebula' (single-tenant) on model redwood-open-7b-stream. p95=310ms p99=2.3s. Streaming stalls observed: 47% streaming sessions with >3s token gap. Detect time 2401234567. SLO p99 < 500ms.

samanthaj: ack — oncall taking. tagging @ryan-sre and @eng-oncall. Any immediate mitigation in flight?

ryan-sre: I'm looking at routing/queue metrics now. Seeing a sharp rise in concurrent live sessions from Nebula starting ~2401234530. Their avg prefix length jumped to ~6.2k tokens (long system prompt + few-shot examples). Batching backlog increased, KV cache eviction rate spiked.

ashwin: long prefixes + high concurrency + continuous batching = KV cache churn. Suggest temporarily disable batching for this customer or pin them to a dedicated pool.

kevin-prod: Nebula is on shared-hosted lane but has single-tenant config flag enabled (logic separation). They hit ~540 concurrent sessions right now, usual is ~60. They reported ramping tests. Can we rate-limit or throttle at the edge?

ryan-sre: Edge throttle in API gateway: we can apply per-customer concurrency cap quickly: `curl -X POST https://internal-gateway/config -d '{"customer":"nebula","max_concurrency":200}'` — will do if approved.

samanthaj: do it. apply 200 cap now and roll back if bad. Also enable fallback to smaller model (redwood-open-3b-q4) for sessions that hit throttle.

ops-bot: RUNBOOK ACTION: applied concurrency cap to nebula -> max_concurrency=200 at 2401234575. Routed overflow to fallback model redwood-open-3b-q4.

ryan-sre: after cap, p95 improved to ~220ms, p99 down to ~760ms but still above SLO. Streaming gaps reduced to 18%. Getting logs for stalled sessions.

ashwin: can we temporarily increase KV cache size for the serving group handling Nebula? If we increase from 8GB -> 16GB, eviction should drop and stalls should reduce. Need eng-runtime to confirm memory headroom.

eng-oncall: checking node memory. There's ~40% headroom on the dedicated infra pool, but autoscaler is conservative. I can bump cache_size for the pool handling Nebula via config toggle: `PUT /runtime/pools/nebula/cache_size?gb=16` — will do once ryan gives go.

ryan-sre: go ahead. Also disabling continuous batching for that pool for next 15m: `PUT /runtime/pools/nebula/disable_batching?duration=15m`.

ops-bot: ACTION: increased cache_size to 16GB at 2401234590. Disabled continuous batching for nebula pool for 15m at 2401234592.

kevin-prod: reaching out to Nebula CSM to warn about throttling and fallback. Sending status page note. No evidence of data loss; only increased latency and streaming stalls.

samanthaj: good. quick customer impact: partial degradation for sessions >3s; about 12% of their sessions experienced visible stalls to end users during peak window. We should include this in the incident summary.

ryan-sre: after cache bump + disable batching + concurrency cap, p99 stabilized ~420ms at 2401234610. Streaming stalls back under 5%. Marking mitigation successful.

ashwin: follow-up items: (1) add an automatic per-customer long-prefix detector that triggers proactive cap / fallback; (2) consider KV cache hot partitioning for single-tenant heavy prefixes; (3) add telemetry to correlate prefix length distribution with cache evictions.

eng-oncall: logging collected: `kvcache_evictions`, `batch_backlog_ms`, `stream_token_gap_histogram`, `pool_memory_usage`. Saving collectors to S3 path `s3://prod-incidents/2401234567/`.

ops-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: mitigated - initial customer-visible impact remediated. Owners: @ryan-sre (mitigation), @ashwin (root-cause analysis), @kevin-prod (customer comms). Will file postmortem and schedule follow-up RCA.

kevin-prod: CSM updated Nebula at 2401234618; they're going to pause their internal ramp tests for now.

samanthaj: handing off to oncall rotation for full RCA. @ashwin you'll lead. I'm closing the live page but leaving thread open for postmortem notes. :white_check_mark:

ashwin: noted. I'll collect traces and kvcache profiles, run repro locally with long prefix generator, and draft RCA. Expected ETA for draft: EOD tomorrow.

incident-bot: INCIDENT CLOSED: runtime mitigation successful, no SLA credit yet. Severity: S2. Start 2401234567 End 2401234620.
